passages.note: Bill overview lists her as a co-sponsor of the single-subject athletics bill and records its passage and signature.
House Third Reading roll call shows her Y vote; only one Bolick appears in the list, and the 31-24 split is far from near-unanimous.

passages.provision_quote: Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex.
passages.note: Chaptered text prints the operative provision; subsection C leaves boys' and coed teams open, so it is not a ban from all sport.

rows.reasoning: Bolick co-sponsored SB 1165 (2022) and voted Y on House Third Reading of this single-subject athletics act, whose operative section designates teams by biological sex and provides that teams designated for "females", "women" or "girls" "may not be open to students of the male sex". That matches the rung that would "require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth". The rung that would "completely ban all transgender athletes from competing in any organized sports competitions" is excluded by the act's own subsection C, which does not restrict participation on teams designated "males", "men" or "boys" or "coed" or "mixed".
